'''Camille-Christophe Gerono''' (1799 in [[Paris, France]] – 1891 in Paris) was a French [[mathematician]]. He concerned himself above all with [[geometry]]. The [[Lemniscate of Gerono]] or ''figure-eight curve'' was named after him.<ref>{{citation|title=Modern Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces with Mathematica|first=Mary|last=Gray|edition=2nd|publisher=CRC Press|year=1997|isbn= 9780849371646 |page=31|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-LRumtTimYgC&pg=PA31}}.</ref> With [[Olry Terquem]], he was founding co-editor in 1842 of the [[scientific journal]] ''[[Nouvelles Annales de Mathématiques]]''.<ref>{{citation|contribution=Terquem, Olry|title=Jewish Encyclopedia|year=1906|publisher=Funk and Wagnalls|url=http://jewishencyclopedia.com/articles/14337-terquem-olry}}.</ref>
